headline: Mathematics Counts More Than Answers
lede: Terence Tao asks mathematics to measure what survives a proof: understanding, exposition, collaboration, and new directions. In an age of machine-generated results, correctness is necessary—but not sufficient.
pullquote: A solved problem is not the same as understood mathematics.

headline: Anthropic Makes Haiku Faster and Cheaper
lede: Claude Haiku 5.5 targets high-volume work with stronger reasoning, coding, browser use, and adjustable effort. Anthropic also cuts selected cache-read costs and sharply lowers pricing for shorter prompts.

headline: A Lost Band Emerges From the Archive
lede: For fifteen years, a search followed scraps of chart data, abandoned webpages, barcode records, and memory. The trail finally identifies Salvage—and restores a small piece of online music history.

headline: Hundred Rabbits Builds a Smaller World
lede: A sailboat becomes a studio, workshop, and laboratory for durable tools. Hundred Rabbits documents repairs, offline software, low-powered hardware, and the practical freedoms—and dependencies—of constrained living.

headline: Margaret Hamilton Leaves a Reliable Legacy
lede: Hamilton, who led Apollo’s flight-software development, died at 90. Her defensive programming and fault-tolerant systems helped turn software engineering into a discipline capable of carrying a mission through failure.

headline: GPT-6 Turns Answers Into Interfaces
lede: OpenAI’s new model can assemble text, charts, forms, and interactive tools around a user’s task. The promise is a quieter interface that adapts itself; the open questions concern reliability, accessibility, and platform control.

headline: The Demoscene Runs Native in Browsers
lede: Demoscene-recomp translates recorded x86 execution paths into cycle-accurate C, alongside models of vintage VGA and Sound Blaster hardware. The result preserves the original software while making its constraints playable again.

headline: Rosalind Franklin Saw the Helix Earlier
lede: A new reading of Franklin’s notes and X-ray images challenges the familiar story surrounding Photograph 51. The evidence suggests she recognized the helical structure before the image became a landmark of molecular biology.

headline: Jonathan Reaches 194 Years
lede: Jonathan the Aldabra tortoise is estimated to be 194 years old, and his genome offers clues to unusually durable biology. Researchers found signals involving DNA repair, mitochondria, telomeres, and cellular cleanup—but no shortcut to human longevity.

headline: When Machines Flood Mathematics With Proofs
lede: Scott Aaronson examines a release of hundreds of AI-generated mathematical arguments, some backed by Lean certificates but many still unread and unverified by mathematicians. The harder question is not only whether the proofs are correct, but how a field learns from work it cannot yet understand.
